findings.title: Hash chain is tamper-evident only against naive edits; no signature, anchor, or signed head, so a full re-hash rewrite o
findings.claim: Certificate Transparency and Rekor make the log head a signed, timestamped commitment (STH/checkpoint) that third-party monitors and witnesses cross-check, and use consistency proofs to prove append-only. CWS has a bare SHA-256 chain with no key, so anyone with write access (the AI agent it polices) can rewrite history and recompute every hash, or truncate the tail. docs/spec.md section 2 admits this, but verify/status output reads as stronger. Guarantees actually delivered: detection of in-place edits/reordering of a prefix, given an honestly held later hash. NOT authenticity, NOT completeness, NOT non-repudiation.
findings.fix: Store the head hash outside the agent's write reach (git tag/commit trailer, or an Ed25519-signed checkpoint {seq, headHash, time} with the key in the OS keyring) and have verify compare against the latest checkpoint; word output as 'chain consistent', not 'untampered'. Copy CT's signed-tree-head idea; drop full Merkle trees (overkill for a single-writer log).

findings.title: Event hash input is JSON.stringify of a nested payload, not a canonical serialisation, and has no domain-separation tag
findings.claim: canonicalEventString fixes only top-level key order; payload and actor are stringified in insertion order. A re-serialiser (Firestore map round-trip in cws sync, a browser/other-language reader for the planned web/ dashboard) can legitimately reorder keys and break verification. Standards: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme; CT RFC 9162 prefixes leaf/node hashes with 0x00/0x01 for second-preimage resistance. CWS preimage is prevHash+JSON with no tag or framing.
findings.fix: Adopt JCS (the small 'canonicalize' package) behind hash schema v:2 and prefix the preimage with a constant such as 'cws-event-v1\0'. Ship cross-implementation test vectors.

findings.title: Append uses a lock file plus in-memory fold, not an expected-version contract; stale-lock takeover is ~120 lines of cust
findings.claim: EventStoreDB/Kurrent and Marten expose expected stream revision/version so a writer that decided against state N fails if the stream moved. CWS appendLocked re-reads under lock and applies the input to whatever state exists now, so a command decided on stale state (human reviewed proposal 5 while another actor changed it) is still appended. Lock recovery (acquireRecovery/takeOver) reimplements what proper-lockfile offers. appendFile is not followed by fsync, so a crash can lose an acknowledged event.
findings.fix: Add optional expectedSeq to append/appendBatch; commands that act on displayed state (accept, decide, review) pass the seq they showed. Consider proper-lockfile. fsync the file handle after append.

findings.title: safe-run is a hand-written denylist over argv; it neither parses shell nor models expansion, and Claude Code's own docs
findings.claim: Claude Code evaluates deny>ask>allow, splits compound commands on && || ; | |& & and newlines (parsed; includes subshells and $(...)), strips a fixed wrapper list, treats unparseable input as not-allowed, and states a deny rule 'isn't a security boundary around the program'; the real boundary is the OS sandbox (Codex: workspace-write, network off by default, .git/.agents/.codex read-only). CWS: SHELL_OPERATORS omits single '&', newline, backtick and '$('; delete targets are not checked for $VAR, ~, %VAR% expansion (hasWildcard tests only * ? [ ] { }); the verdict is documented as often retyped into a real shell, where all of that applies. Bypass literature: CVE-2025-55284 (Claude Code <1.0.4, over-broad allowlist let read-then-exfil skip prompts); Claude docs on argument-pattern fragility (curl with variables, redirects).
findings.fix: (a) Fail closed on any of [&\n\r`$%~] unless runsWithoutShell is true. (b) For shell strings, parse with tree-sitter-bash (node binding) or bashlex-class parser and walk every command node including substitutions; reject on parse error. (c) Reword UX from 'safe' to 'no known destructive pattern' and make the OS/OpenShell sandbox the stated boundary. Drop: the growing LAUNCHERS list as a security claim.

findings.title: Allow-by-default for unknown commands ('no destructive filesystem pattern detected')
findings.claim: Claude Code and Codex are default-ask/default-deny with a small read-only allowlist. CWS inverts it: anything not matched by LAUNCHERS, COMMAND_RULES or DELETE_COMMANDS returns ok:true, e.g. dd, truncate, chmod -R, mkfs, sed -i, tee, cp -f overwrite, curl -o over a file. A denylist can never be complete.
findings.fix: For AI actors, allowlist known read-only/safe commands; everything else needs the human challenge code CWS already has.

findings.title: Redaction is nine regexes plus a keyword=value rule; no entropy detector, allowlist/baseline or verification; only inges
findings.claim: gitleaks = provider rules + keyword prefilter + Shannon-entropy thresholds + allowlists + baseline; detect-secrets adds entropy and keyword plugins and an audited baseline; trufflehog (800+ detectors) live-verifies and reports verified/unverified/unknown. CWS covers AKIA, GitHub, sk-, Slack xox, JWT, AIza, glpat, npm, PEM and name=value credentials with 4+ chars. Misses Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, Azure keys, bare high-entropy tokens, DSNs without scheme, prose ('password is hunter2'). The log is append-only and hash-chained, so a leaked secret cannot be removed without breaking the chain, and cws sync pushes whole events to Firestore.
findings.fix: Do not hand-maintain: vendor gitleaks default rules (MIT) or shell out to gitleaks/detect-secrets as an optional integration; add an entropy fallback in key-like contexts; scan on EVERY write path (note, claim, evidence, decision) and before sync push and before Gemini; define a redaction tombstone event convention since history cannot be rewritten. Skip live verification (it sends the secret to vendors).

findings.title: Sync uses the Firebase web SDK in a CLI but never signs the SDK in; the stored 'refreshToken' is an arbitrary pasted str
findings.claim: Firebase: Admin SDK is for privileged servers and bypasses Security Rules; client SDKs obey rules but need an authenticated user (signInWithCredential / signInWithCustomToken, or the securetoken REST refresh exchange). CWS initialises the web SDK with only {projectId:'cws-base'}, no apiKey and no auth, then reads/writes users/{uid}/..., so every call has request.auth == null and the owner-only rules deny it. loginWithToken accepts any string, decodes the JWT body without signature or exp check to pick uid, and stores it as refreshToken though an ID token is not a refresh token and lasts 1 hour. Net: cws sync as written cannot pass the deployed rules, or, if rules are loosened to test, trusts a client-asserted uid.
findings.fix: Use the installed-app flow: OAuth 2.0 loopback or device code with PKCE, exchange via Identity Toolkit signInWithIdp, keep the Firebase refresh token, mint ID tokens via securetoken.googleapis.com, then REST with the ID token or signInWithCredential. Take uid from the server response, never a decoded token. Alternative that removes the class: a small Cloud Function you control using Admin SDK.

findings.title: Refresh token stored as plaintext JSON; mode 0o600 is a no-op on Windows and the directory is created with default mode;
findings.claim: Common CLI practice is the OS credential store. keytar is archived (2022-12-15); the maintained drop-in is @napi-rs/keyring (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service/keyutils). clig.dev: do not read secrets from flags (visible in ps and shell history).
findings.fix: Store the token via @napi-rs/keyring (optional dependency; file fallback with chmod 600 plus warning, icacls on Windows). Replace --token with stdin/--token-file. Logout should also revoke the token, not just unlink.

findings.title: Rules claim an append-only immutable ledger but the project meta doc (headSeq/headHash) is freely writable and deletable
findings.claim: 'allow write' on /projects/{id} permits create, update and delete, so the head pointer that status/push/pull trust can be rewritten or removed. events/{seq} create does not check document id == padSeq(data.seq), seq == previous+1, or prevHash == previous doc's hash (rules can get() the neighbour). Two devices pushing concurrently both pass the client-side ancestry check; the loser gets an opaque batch failure. Pushes over 450 events are several batches with meta only in the last, so a mid-way failure leaves events beyond headSeq. Replicache (server-authoritative push with mutation ids) and Automerge treat concurrent writers as the normal case.
findings.fix: Rules: meta create+update only, headSeq monotonic, delete false; require seq doc id match and get()-based prevHash check. Use a transaction/precondition on meta as compare-and-swap. Keep pull-time chain verification (already good).

findings.title: Sync is fast-forward only; any divergence is a dead end (no merge or rebase path) despite the multi-device goal
findings.claim: Automerge merges concurrent offline edits; Replicache rewinds to server state and replays pending mutations (rebase). For a hash-chained linear log a CRDT is the wrong tool, but CWS offers neither rebase nor guidance: only 'DIVERGED, nothing pushed' and the destructive import --replace. Events are intents, so replaying local events onto the remote head with new seq/hash and re-validating authority is feasible.
findings.fix: Do NOT adopt a CRDT. Add 'cws sync rebase' (find fork, replay local events as new ones, surface conflicts through existing validators). State plainly in README that Firestore is a mirror, not a merge engine.

findings.title: ADRs are free-form markdown with no machine-checked status lifecycle, supersession links, date or deciders, and are disc
findings.claim: adr-tools 'adr new -s N' writes the new ADR and flips the old one to superseded; MADR standardises status (proposed|rejected|accepted|deprecated|superseded by ADR-NNNN), date, decision-makers, drivers, considered options with pros/cons, consequences and a Confirmation section; log4brains publishes a searchable site and derives metadata from git (it does not lint). CWS ADR 0001-0003 use ad-hoc Status/Context/Options/Decision/Consequences, no deciders, no supersedes, no confirmation. The repo thus has two decision systems.
findings.fix: Copy MADR frontmatter and the Confirmation section; add 'cws decision export --madr'. Skip log4brains site. Add a verify:repo check that every ADR has a valid status and supersede links are bidirectional.

findings.title: Context pack and agent protocol are monolithic and unbudgeted, unlike the scoped, size-bounded memory in Claude Code and
findings.claim: Claude Code: CLAUDE.md under ~200 lines, path-scoped .claude/rules load only for matching files, @imports depth 4, auto-memory loads first 200 lines/25KB, and the docs say memory is context, not enforcement (use a PreToolUse hook). Aider loads CONVENTIONS.md read-only so it is prompt-cached. Cline's memory bank has six fixed files with a hot activeContext.md. CWS renders the whole state into one pack with no budget, ranking or cache-stable prefix; its rule that agents only use --agent commands is instruction text.
findings.fix: Add --budget with ranked inclusion (open risks, falsified premises, recent decisions first); put the stable protocol first and volatile state last for caching; ship a PreToolUse hook template in install-agents. Copy Cline's 'active context' as a derived view; drop hand-edited memory files (the event log is the better source).

findings.title: No change-delta or spec-vs-implementation convergence loop as in OpenSpec / spec-kit; log is opaque to humans compared w
findings.claim: OpenSpec separates specs/ (truth) from changes/ (proposal, ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED delta, tasks) and archives on completion; spec-kit has constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement and a convergence check. CWS has no first-class claim -> requirement -> test/finding link; SUPPORTED_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE is the only coverage check. Basic Memory keeps observations and typed relations in human-editable markdown plus a SQLite index; events.jsonl is not human-readable.
findings.fix: Copy the delta idea as a derived 'changes since phase X' view and a read-only markdown export of state. Drop MCP/vector search (spec section 7 rightly defers it).

findings.title: No machine-readable output: --json exists only as an input flag; no --no-input, NO_COLOR/--no-color handling, or documen
findings.claim: clig.dev: --json output, primary output to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, honour NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb/non-TTY, provide --no-input, never take secrets via flags, map non-zero codes to failure modes. CWS has good exit codes (EXIT OK/ERROR/NEEDS_HUMAN/INTEGRITY) and stderr errors, but only propose has --json (input); status, verify, doctor, findings have none, and interactivity is inferred only from TTY, so agents cannot parse output and humans cannot force non-interactive mode.
findings.fix: Add global --json (versioned schema) for status, verify, doctor, context, findings list, sync status; add --no-input and NO_COLOR handling now; document exit codes in --help and README.

findings.title: Consent to send project memory to Gemini is a one-time yes/no with no preview of what leaves, while masking is regex-onl
findings.claim: Claude Code and Codex gate each egress class and show the action; secret scanners run before egress. CWS offers no dry-run of the outgoing pack, no per-project consent event, no per-kind inclusion control.
findings.fix: Add 'cws ai --dry-run' printing the exact pack and size, record consent per project as an event, and refuse to send if the O-6 scanner flags anything.
